2008–09 All-Big East Tournament first team }} '''Devin Ebanks''' (born October 28, 1989 in [[Long Island City, Queens|Long Island City]], [[New York]]) is a [[basketball]] player. He is a sophomore [[forward (basketball)|forward]] at [[West Virginia Mountaineers|West Virginia University]]. Ebanks is projected as a mid-first-round [[2010 NBA Draft]] prospect.{{cite web|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/2010mock_draft |title=2010 Mock Draft |publisher=NBADraft.net |date= |accessdate=April 2, 2010}} ==High school career== As a sophomore at Bishop Loughlin High in [[Brooklyn]], [[New York]], Ebanks averaged 18 points, six rebounds and 1.3 assists per game. In his junior season, at St. Thomas More School in [[Connecticut]], he averaged 23 points, five rebounds, four assists, and three steals. In his senior season, Ebanks recorded an average of 23 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists per game at More. He scored over 1,000 points in his two seasons at St. Thomas More. Ebanks received various honors while a prep player in high school. These honors included the [[Michael Jordan|Jordan Brand Classic All-Star Game]] in New York, playing [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball, and being one of 30 players selected for the 2007 USA Basketball Development Festival at the [[Olympics|U.S. Olympic]] Training Center in [[Colorado Springs, Colorado]]. While at the camp, Ebanks averaged 28.2 points and 4.8 rebounds per game. Ebanks was widely regarded as one of the top high school players in the nation by scouting services, ranking 11th overall and 13th overall in the class by Rivals.com and Scout.com, respectively.{{cite web|url=http://www.msnsportsnet.com/profile.cfm?id=101739&sport=mbball |title=West Virginia University Mountaineers |publisher=MSNsportsNET.Com |date= |accessdate=April 2, 2010}} He was being pursured by various colleges, such as [[Indiana Hoosiers|Indiana]], [[Memphis Tigers|Memphis]], [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights|Rutgers]], and [[Texas Longhorns|Texas]].{{cite web|url=http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?pr_key=41968&Sport=2 |title=Devin Ebanks - Yahoo! Sports |publisher=Rivalshoops.rivals.com |date=May 18, 2008 |accessdate=April 2, 2010}} Ebanks originally signed with the Indiana Hoosiers, but was released from his letter of intent after coach [[Kelvin Sampson]] was dismissed. Ebanks signed his letter of intent with [[Bob Huggins|Bob Huggins']] [[West Virginia University]]. ==Collegiate career== ===Freshman season=== Listed as one of the Top 15 impact freshman by [[Sports Illustrated]] coming into the 2008–2009 season, Ebanks began his campaign as a starter at forward in the 92–47 victory over [[Elon University|Elon]]. Ebanks scored 9 points and grabbed 3 rebounds in his first collegiate game and start. In the following 86–54 win over [[Longwood University|Longwood]], Ebanks scored 7 points and grabbed 7 rebounds. As the Mountaineers then defeated [[Delaware State]] to begin the Las Vegas Invitational Tournament, he scored 8 points and grabbed 4 boards. In the 87–68 win over [[Iowa Hawkeyes|Iowa]], he totaled 7 points and 2 rebounds in fourteen minutes of playing time. West Virginia then lost to [[Kentucky Wildcats|Kentucky]] 54–43, in which Ebanks scored 4 points and only had one rebound. In the following 80–78 win over [[Ole Miss|Mississippi]], Ebanks recorded no points but did have 3 boards and a blocked shot. Ebanks totaled a then season-high 17 rebounds to go along with his 10 points, 3 assists, 3 steals, and 2 blocks in the win over [[Cleveland State University|Cleveland State]].[http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/player/gamelog?playerId=41840&year=2009 Devin Ebanks West Virginia Mountaineers Game Log (2008–09)] In the following 68–65 loss to #22 [[Davidson University|Davidson]] in [[Madison Square Garden]], Ebanks led the team with 17 rebounds and also had 13 points. He then followed up in the [[Duquesne University|Duquesne]] win with his third double-double: 15 points and 10 rebounds. However, his run was ended as he missed the majority of the Miami University victory with an injury. Ebanks bounced back with 9 points and 10 rebounds in the win over [[Radford University|Radford]]. In the 76–48 win over [[Ohio State Buckeyes|Ohio State]], Ebanks had 10 points and 5 rebounds. In the following win over [[Seton Hall]], Ebanks had 10 points and 9 rebounds. He played 25 minutes of the loss to #1 [[Connecticut Huskies|UConn]], however he only had 4 points and 2 rebounds; in the following loss to [[Marquette University|Marquette]] Ebanks had 8 points and 3 rebounds. In the win over rival [[Marshall Thundering Herd|Marshall]], he totaled 12 points and 4 rebounds, then 5 points and 10 rebounds in the win over [[South Florida Bulls|USF]]. In the following win over [[Georgetown Hoyas|Georgetown]], Ebanks had 9 points and 7 rebounds. In the loss to [[Pittsburgh Panthers|Pittsburgh]] in the [[Backyard Brawl]], Ebanks had 9 points and 5 rebounds. In the following win over [[St. John's University (New York)|St. John's]], he had 10 points and 8 rebounds. In the 69–63 loss to [[Louisville Cardinals|Louisville]], Ebanks had 14 points and 6 rebounds. As the Mountaineers lost to [[Syracuse Orangemen|Syracuse]], he recorded 9 points and 9 rebounds. In the 86–59 win over [[Providence University|Providence]], he had 13 points and 6 rebounds. In the second loss to Pittsburgh, he totaled a season-high 16 points with 7 rebounds. He followed the seaosn-high point-performance with a double-double in the victory over [[Villanova University|Villanova]] – 16 points and 10 rebounds. In the 79–68 win over [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish|Notre Dame]], Ebanks recorded 11 points and 9 rebounds. In the following win over [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights|Rutgers]], Ebanks had another double-double with 14 points and 11 rebounds. Ebanks had a consecutive double-double in the loss to [[Cincinnati Bearcats|Cincinnati]] with 12 points and 14 rebounds. He then had 10 points and 7 rebounds in a victory over South Florida. Ebanks had his 9th double-double of his rookie campaign in the win over [[DePaul]] with 14 points and 14 rebounds. Ebanks ended the regular season against #6 [[Louisville Cardinals|Louisville]] with a season-high 16 points and 10 rebounds for his 10th double-double of the season. Following the 62–59 loss, Ebanks was named to the All-[[Big East]] rookie team.{{cite web|url=http://westvirginia.scout.com/2/845459.html |title=Scout.com: Three Mountaineers Earn Big East Awards |publisher=Westvirginia.scout.com |date=March 8, 2009 |accessdate=April 2, 2010}} In the second round of the Big East Tournament against Notre Dame, Ebanks scored 7 points and had 5 assists to go with his season-high 18 rebounds. In the following round, defeating the #2 [[Pittsburgh Panthers]] 74–60, Ebanks had a season-high 20 points with 7 rebounds and 3 assists. In the semifinals, he led the team to overtime against #20 [[Syracuse Orangemen|Syracuse]], setting a new career-high with 22 points and he also had 6 rebounds, 3 assists and 3 steals in the 74–69 loss. Ebanks was named to the first team All-Big East Tournament squad with his average of 16 points and 10 rebounds during the tenure. However, the Mountaineers lost in the first round of the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] to [[University of Dayton|Dayton]], 68–60, with Ebanks scoring 14 points and grabbing 12 rebounds. For his true freshman season, Ebanks averaged 10.5 points and 7.8 rebounds per game in his starting role. He had season-highs of 22 points against Syracuse and 18 rebounds against Notre Dame. Ebanks finished the year with double-point figures in 12 of his last 13 games with six double-doubles in those games.{{cite web|url=http://www.msnsportsnet.com/page.cfm?story=14405&cat=exclusives |title=West Virginia University Mountaineers |publisher=MSNsportsNET.Com |date=March 20, 2009 |accessdate=April 2, 2010}} After some speculation, Ebanks has announced he will return for his sophomore season.{{cite web|url=http://www.msnsportsnet.com/page.cfm?cat=netnews&story=14533 |title=West Virginia University Mountaineers |publisher=MSNsportsNET.Com |date=April 13, 2009 |accessdate=April 2, 2010}} ==Notes== ==External links== *[http://www.msnsportsnet.com/profile.cfm?id=101739&sport=mbball WVU Profile] *[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=41840 ESPN Player Card] *[http://wvustats.com/mbasketball/player.php?team_id=308&person_id=52557 WVU Stats] {{DEFAULTSORT:Ebanks, Devin}} [[Category:1989 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:African American basketball players]] [[Category:West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from New Jersey]] [[Category:Basketball players from New York]] [[Category:People from Newark, New Jersey]] [[Category:Small forwards]]
